subject: gk
question: Which of the following statements about plastids is INCORRECT?

options.text: Leucoplasts are primarily organelles in which materials such as starch, oils and protein granules are stored.
Leucoplasts are white or colourless plastids.
Plastids do not have their own DNA and ribosomes.
Chromoplasts are responsible for photosynthesis in plants.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Plastids do not have their own DNA and ribosomes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plastids, including chloroplasts, leucoplasts, and chromoplasts, do contain their own DNA and ribosomes.
 
• Plastid DNA is circular and similar to bacterial DNA, reflecting their evolutionary origin.
 
• Due to their own DNA and ribosomes, plastids can produce some of their own proteins independently of the cell's nuclear DNA.
 
• The presence of their own genetic material is a key feature distinguishing plastids from other organelles like the endoplasmic reticulum or Golgi apparatus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Leucoplasts**

 
 
• They are colorless plastids found in non-photosynthetic tissues of plants.
 
• Primarily involved in the storage of starch, oils, and proteins.
 
• Leucoplasts can differentiate into other forms of plastids based on the plant’s needs.
 
 
 
• **Chromoplasts**
 
 
• Chromoplasts contain pigments like carotenoids, which give yellow, red, and orange colors to various plant parts.
 
• They are involved in the synthesis and storage of pigments, aiding in the process of pollination by attracting pollinators.
 
 
 
• **Chloroplasts**
 
 
• Chloroplasts are green plastids responsible for photosynthesis in plant cells.
 
• They contain chlorophyll, which captures light energy for the synthesis of glucose.
 
• Chloroplasts have their own DNA and ribosomes, similar to other plastids.
 
 
 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory**
 
 
• This theory explains the origin of plastids and mitochondria as formerly free-living prokaryotes that were engulfed by early eukaryotic cells.
 
• Both organelles have their own circular DNA and ribosomes similar to bacteria, supporting this theory.
